Article Title: Brij Bhushan acquittal challenged over ‘stereotypical assumptions’ about sexual assault victims
Article Text:
Wrestlers challenge acquittal, cite ‘stereotypical assumptions’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue court has issued notice to former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and others on an appeal challenging his acquittal in a sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers.Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on October 9. The court also directed that the original affidavit and orders containing the names of the victims be placed in a sealed envelope. It further directed the appellant to file a copy of the petition with the victims’ names redacted.The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case. The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a “manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on record”.The appeal has contended that the impugned order proceeds on conjectures and surmises, fails to apply binding and well-settled principles of law, and, in material part, rests its reasoning on “archaic and stereotypical assumptions” about the “expected” behaviour of victims of sexual assault and harassment, rather than on a fair, evidence-based assessment after taking into account the circumstances of the victims.The case stems from an FIR filed by Delhi Police following a complaint by a woman wrestler during Singh’s tenure as WFI chief. The police had invoked Sections 354, 354-D, 354-A, 506(1) and 109 of the Indian Penal Code.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar had acquitted Singh and Tomar after a trial that was conducted in a closed courtroom. The two were tried in connection with allegations of sexual harassment of women wrestlers in India and abroad.Delhi Police had filed a 1,500-page charge sheet against Singh and Tomar on June 15, 2023, following its investigation into the allegations.The women wrestlers had earlier staged a protest at Jantar Mantar, following which the FIR was registered by Delhi Police based on the complaint.Advocate Rajiv Mohan, assisted by Rehan Khan and Rishabh Bhati, represented Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, while senior advocate Rebecca John appeared for the victims and complainants.
Article Summary: Wrestlers challenge acquittal, cite ‘stereotypical assumptions’ special judge dig vinay singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on october 9. The appeal challenges the august 3 order of the rouse avenue court, brij bhushan and vinod tomar in the case.

Article Title: “An F”: Caitlin Clark accepts failure as Indiana Fever crushed by Aces in A'ja Wilson's 38-point showdown
Article Text:
Caitlin Clark reacts to Fever's loss against Aces. Image via: Getty Images

Why Caitlin Clark gave the Fever defense an F in Game 1

Raven Johnson gives Caitlin Clark and the Fever one bright spot

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Caitlin Clark kept her postgame review short. Asked to grade the Indiana Fever defense, she said, "An F." Few could argue.The Las Vegas Aces took the first-round opener 102-85 on Sunday, and A'ja Wilson did most of the damage with 38 points and 16 rebounds. Indiana now has one game left to keep its season alive, and the defense needs a lot of work before then.Caitlin Clark's grade came after the Fever allowed 102 points on Sunday, and the numbers back it up. Las Vegas shot 59 percent overall and 47 percent from three. It was one of those nights when nearly every possession ended in a clean look.Wilson was the center of it all. The reigning WNBA MVP hit 15 of 19 shots and tied a playoff career high with 38 points. She also pulled down 16 rebounds, blocked four shots, stole the ball twice, handed out two assists and knocked down two threes. Indiana had no real answer for her.The Fever guard had a rough night at the other end too. Clark scored 15 points on 6-of-17 shooting, though she did add 10 assists for a double-double. Kelsey Mitchell struggled even more, hitting 4 of 16 for 12 points. Aliyah Boston led Indiana with 18, and Sophie Cunningham chipped in 13 off the bench.It was not enough to keep pace with an Aces offense that barely missed.Indiana lost backup guard Tyasha Harris to a season-ending leg injury in the last regular-season game. Coach Stephanie White had said before the playoffs that rookie Raven Johnson could help fill the gap. She did.Johnson played 22 minutes off the bench in the postseason debut and scored 14 points on 6-of-7 shooting. She added two steals, an assist and a three-pointer. The two-time NCAA champion at South Carolina looked comfortable on a night when few teammates did. White said Johnson "did great" and gave the team the lift it needed on both ends.Clark, the newly crowned AP Comeback Player of the Year, was just as impressed with the 5-foot-8 rookie. She liked the offense, but she singled out the defensive intensity as exactly what Indiana needs from here on. In her view, Johnson puts in the work and can be counted on.Now the margin is gone. Game 2 is Tuesday at Gainbridge Fieldhouse, with tipoff set for 6:30 p.m. ET. A second loss ends the Fever's season. Clark and her teammates will need far more resistance against Wilson and an Aces attack that hit almost everything in Game 1.
Article Summary: Caitlin clark gave the indiana fever defense an f in game 1. A'ja wilson did most of the damage with 38 points and 16 rebounds. Game 2 is tuesday at gainbridge fieldhouse, with tipoff set for 6:30 p.m. Et.

Article Title: AEW confirms PAC death at 40: British star Benjamin Satterley dies as details surrounding his passing remain unclear
Article Text:
Benjamin Satterley dies at 40. Image via: Instagram/thepacwrestling

PAC cause of death: what is known so far

Beyond the PAC cause of death: a career built on high-flying offense

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The PAC cause of death has not been disclosed, and fans are left with more questions than facts. All Elite Wrestling announced on social media on Sunday night that Benjamin Satterley had died at 40. The statement gave no details about how or where.The news hit hard because of how close it came to All Out. The two-time cruiserweight champion had worked the opening match in Chicago on Saturday night, a National Championship challenge against Andrade El Idolo, and lost. Then came Sunday's brief, heartbreaking announcement.Benjamin Satterley's death was announced by AEW on Sunday night, first through its social media accounts.The questions are loud because the calendar is so tight. PAC worked All Out in Chicago on Saturday, opening the show against Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship.In its statement, AEW posted a heartfelt tribute. "All Elite Wrestling is saddened to announce the passing of Benjamin Satterley, aka Pac. A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability."Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history.Our condolences go out to Satterley’s family, friends and fans."Until AEW, his family or an official source says more, any explanation is a guess.Satterley started in the ring in 2004 and spent the 2000s building a name on the international circuit. WWE signed him in 2012. Working as Neville, he became a standout in NXT, where his Red Arrow finisher drew big reactions. Yahoo Sports recalls his tagline, "The Man That Gravity Forgot," which suited his style.The titles followed. He held the NXT Championship, won the NXT tag team titles twice and took the cruiserweight title twice. He is the only two-time WWE cruiserweight champion and the longest-reigning one.His WWE exit is told two ways. A reported walkout during a Raw taping in 2017, while Yahoo Sports lists his release in 2018. Either way, the Newcastle native spent about a year on the independent circuit before joining AEW in 2019 and returning to the PAC name.In AEW, he became the first All-Atlantic Champion, a belt now called the International Championship. He also won the World Trios titles twice, teaming with Penta and Rey Fenix as Death Triangle. He spent his final days with the Death Riders.It has been a heavy year for the promotion. Fans are still far from moving on from the death of former AEW wrestler Andy Williams, known as The Butcher, earlier in 2026.

Article Title: "You’re teaching them the blueprint every day”: LeBron James opens up on raising his three children with Savannah James
Article Text:
LeBron James opens up.(Image via Getty Images)

LeBron James reflects on parenting three children with wife Savannah James and how he has been teaching them about life

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

LeBron James inspires many with the way he has stepped up to be there for his three children

LeBron James, the NBA legend, has been on the court for over two decades and is easily one of the richest and popular athletes in the world. While the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon has had a stellar career in the league, he never forgot to be a dedicated and a present parent to his three children who he shares with his wife, Savannah James.As LeBron James gears up for the new season on the court with the Philadelphia 76ers, his words on parenting have resurfaced.A few years ago, in an interview with WKYC's Amani Abraham, LeBron James opened up about how he teaches his three children about life as he said, "It's an every day thing…”The four time NBA champion added, “It's not like I sit my kids down and be like, 'Listen, this is what I'm telling you, this is how you should do...' No. It's every day...You're teaching them the blueprint every day."The former Los Angeles Lakers’ star player continued, "It's how you walk, it's how you get up, it's how you respect people in your household…I believe, not only for myself, but for my wife, for my mom, for my [in-laws], and everyone in our family, we're just trying to set a great example not only in the household, but when you leave the household."The 41 year old NBA icon LeBron James added, "I have a lot of gems to give," he said, "but I think it has to be spread across time and along the whole tier of [when] they're growing up, and not just give it to them all at once."Over the last two decades, the world has seen how LeBron James stepped up to be there for his three children and take fatherhood seriously even though he was just a young adult when he had his oldest son, Bronny James.Since LeBron James grew up without a father figure in his life, he has always tried to fulfil his role and give his children the support and love he never got from his father.In many interviews, LeBron James’ wife Savannah James has reflected on how he never hesitated to be a parent when they discovered that they were expecting Bronny James at a pretty young age.At this point in time, all eyes remain on the NBA icon LeBron James as he focuses on his last season in the court before taking a retirement with the Philadelphia 76ers.

Article Title: Sophie Cunningham’s sensational cheetah-print look fails to dim Fever’s devastating loss as Aces advance in playoff battle
Article Text:
Sophie Cunningham at Michelob ULTRA Arena. Image via Getty Images

Why Sophie Cunningham's cheetah coat could not lift the Fever in Game 1

Sophie Cunningham's cheetah coat. Image via: Getty Images

Sophie Cunningham faces a $500 fine after the Chelsea Gray foul

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sophie Cunningham arrived at Michelob ULTRA Arena on Sunday in a long cheetah-print coat and matching shorts, dressed for a playoff opener. The Las Vegas Aces spoiled it fast. They beat the Indiana Fever 102-85 in Game 1 of the first-round series, and A'ja Wilson did most of the damage.A first-quarter flagrant foul on Aces star Chelsea Gray added to the sting, and the 6-foot-1 guard now faces league discipline. Indiana must win Game 2 on Tuesday at home to keep its season alive.Sophie Cunningham has turned the pregame walk into a weekly show for Indiana this season, and Game 1 was no exception. The coat came only days after a sweater that read "Kick Rocks" before the Fever faced the Minnesota Lynx in the second-last game of the regular season.The fashion was the easy part. The Fever had to solve the defending champions on the road, in a best-of-three series, and the Aces gave them no room. Las Vegas has won three of the last four WNBA titles. It finished 31-13 and came up two games short of the top seed. Indiana arrived as the No. 6 seed, hoping a healthier roster would close the gap. Coach Stephanie White had said Aliyah Boston would play after a leg injury, and she did.Wilson made sure the night belonged to Las Vegas. The reigning MVP scored 38 points on 15-of-19 shooting to tie a playoff career high. Wilson also pulled down 16 rebounds, blocked four shots and hit two threes in 35 minutes. Few teams have an answer for that kind of game.Indiana got real work from its stars, just not enough of it. Boston led the team with 18 points and eight rebounds. Caitlin Clark finished with 15 points and 10 assists. Kelsey Mitchell, who set a single-season scoring record this year, had a rough shooting night at 4-of-16 for 12 points.The Fever guard gave the bench a lift with 13 points and three triples on six tries.In the first quarter, Cunningham contested a Gray jumper and, in the officials' view, violated Gray's landing space. The referees first called a common foul. After a replay review, they went another way. ESPN (@espn) shared the result on X: "Sophie Cunningham's foul on Chelsea Gray was upgraded to a Flagrant 1."The cost is small for now. Under WNBA rules, Cunningham is looking at a $500 fine and one flagrant point. If she collects four points across the playoffs, she will sit out a game. Indiana can ill afford that in a short series.The bigger question is what the Fever can fix by Tuesday. Game 2 tips off at Gainbridge Fieldhouse at 6:30 p.m. ET. Indiana has to win to stay alive, and one more Aces victory ends the series.
Article Summary: Sophie cunningham faces a $500 fine after the chelsea gray foul. A'ja wilson scored 38 points on 15-of-19 shooting to tie a playoff career high. Game 2 tips off at gainbridge fieldhouse at 6:30 p.m. Et.

Article Title: Chess Olympiad Round 9: D Gukesh channels his world champion self, overturns almost-lost game to keep India in gold hunt
Article Text:
Dommaraju Gukesh of India (Photo by Rafal Oleksiewicz for FIDE)

How Gukesh turned the tables on Donchenko

Vantika, Divya lead India's women to victory

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

ALSO READ:

NEW DELHI: Since becoming world champion two years ago, noise has followed Dommaraju Gukesh almost everywhere, at times making it feel as though he isn't worthy of the title he rightfully won.But on Friday, when India needed the youngest world champion in history to deliver a win, he did exactly that, turning around an almost-lost position to beat Germany's Alexander Donchenko in Round 9 of the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.It was the kind of performance that felt like it could quiet the criticism all on its own.Playing black, Gukesh traded off his dark-squared bishop early to damage White's pawn structure, then spent the middlegame manoeuvring patiently, repositioning knights, expanding on the queenside with a5-a4, and probing for weaknesses without rushing.For a long stretch, the position stayed murky and roughly balanced, with both sides shuffling pieces and neither able to land a clean blow.It was in the run-up to the time control that things turned dangerous for Gukesh. Donchenko doubled his rooks on the e-file and pushed one all the way to e6, aiming squarely at Black's king, which had been forced to step out to f7 for safety.With his own clock running low, Gukesh had to defend precisely while trying to generate counterplay of his own on the kingside, pushing his h- and g-pawns forward to create complications.It was a position where one careless move could have ended the game in White's favour.Gukesh held his nerve. As the pawn storms and piece trades settled down, he found a route to activate his queen and knight while White's pieces drifted out of coordination.The Chennai-born grandmaster found an excellent move with 51...Nf4. The German sacked Gukesh's knight with 52.Rxf4, but Donchenko's bishop was thus left hanging on c3; Gukesh's queen swooped in to capture it, and from there it was a matter of technique.A check with his queen forced Donchenko's king into an impossible spot, and White resigned rather than play on a piece down with his king exposed.Elsewhere on the board, Nihal Sarin, playing white, spent much of his game in some turmoil against Frederik Svane but held firm for a draw.With Gukesh's win already banked, Praggnanandhaa and Arjun Erigaisi didn't need to force matters either, settling for draws against Vincent Keymer and Matthias Bluebaum, respectively. India closed out the match 2.5-1.5.With the win, India moved to 15 points, still one point behind hosts Uzbekistan, who beat the United States on Friday to stay in front.India's women's team also had a productive Friday, with Vantika Agrawal and Divya Deshmukh both delivering important wins to seal the match against Uzbekistan.Vantika, playing white against Nilufarkhon Imomkuzieva, picked up an early pawn with a sharp tactical sequence; a check with her queen forced Black's king to give up material before the middlegame had properly begun.She nursed that small material edge through a long, technical battle, trading down into a rook endgame where her extra pawn and more active king proved decisive.Pushing her kingside pawns forward in the closing stages, Vantika eventually broke through, and Imomkuzieva had no way to hold the position together.Divya Deshmukh's game against Gulrukhbegim Tokhirjonova was a far longer and more chaotic affair.Both sides grabbed material early. Tokhirjonova's knight snatched a pawn on b7 just as Divya's queen picked up a stray piece on d2, leaving the position roughly balanced but sharp.What followed was a marathon battle through the middlegame and into a complex rook, knight and bishop endgame, with both players navigating tricky technical positions deep into the game.Divya's technique held up better over the long haul, and after 73 hard-fought moves, Tokhirjonova had nothing left to stop Black's advancing king, resigning the position.Those two results were enough to see India through the match, keeping the team firmly in the mix for a medal.As things stand, India's women sit second in the standings on 15 points, behind an in-form Chinese side on 17.With two rounds left, India's hopes of gold now depend largely on whether China slip up, but on Friday's evidence, neither Indian team looks inclined to make things easy for anyone chasing them either.In the Open section, India face Uzbekistan 2, while the women’s team take on China in the penultimate round of the Chess Olympiad.
Article Summary: Dommaraju gukesh beats germany's alexander donchenko in round 9 of the 46th chess olympiad in samarkand, uzbekistan. India's women's team also had a productive friday, with vantika agrawal and divya deshmukh both delivering important wins to seal the match. Tokhirjonova's knight snatched a pawn on b7 just as divya's queen picked up a stray piece on d2.

NEW DELHI: Double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker will return from the Asian Games 2026 without a medal after competing in four events in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan — an unexpected outcome for one of India’s biggest medal hopes and another indication of the shooting contingent’s struggles to match its record haul from the previous edition.India had won 22 shooting medals, including seven gold, at the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2023. In Aichi-Nagoya, the Indian shooters have so far managed 12 medals, with only one gold, with just five trap medal events remaining in the competition. Esha Singh’s silver in the women’s 25m pistol on Monday added to the tally, but the overall campaign has lacked the gold-medal returns India had hoped for.Manu entered the Games as one of India’s biggest medal contenders after her historic double bronze at the Paris Olympics and strong recent international form. But the 24-year-old could not convert her four medal opportunities into a podium finish.Her campaign began with the women’s 10m air pistol events. Manu qualified third for the individual final with 579 points but finished fifth after scoring 181.1 in the medal round. India also narrowly missed a medal in the corresponding team event, finishing fourth.The 25m pistol events offered another opportunity, but Manu missed the individual final after scoring 579-18x in qualification to finish 11th.She then ended her campaign on Monday as India finished fifth in the 25m pistol team event.The Indian trio of Esha Singh, Manu and Rahi Sarnobat scored 1727-56x. China won gold with 1743-68x, South Korea took silver with 1735-65x and Chinese Taipei claimed bronze with 1734-48x.Esha provided a bright spot by winning silver in the individual 25m pistol final after an exhausting series of shoot-offs, giving India another shooting medal.Despite Manu’s disappointment, shooting remains one of India’s most productive disciplines at Aichi-Nagoya. The contingent has delivered 12 medals so far, but the haul includes only one gold, a sharp contrast to the seven gold medals and 22 total shooting medals India collected at Hangzhou.Manu had arrived in Japan in good form. She won bronze at the 2026 ISSF World Cup in Hangzhou, while Esha claimed gold in the women’s 25m pistol at the same event. At the ISSF World Cup in Munich, Manu also won silver in the 10m air pistol mixed team event with Samrat Rana. She subsequently won individual silver in the women’s 25m pistol at the Asian Shooting Championships.Her father, Ram Kishan Bhaker, acknowledged that her performance had fallen below the standards she had established.“Manu's performance was not as per her standard because she set a very high standard and expectation for the Indian fans. As per my expectations, her score must be more than 585; it should be more than 585 to 595. Today's score was not enough...” he told IANS.He also questioned the circumstances surrounding Rahi Sarnobat’s crucial miss in the 25m pistol qualification.“Rahi was shooting very well, but suddenly one shot was not showing, which I believe may be the technical glitch or something else.”“But, later on the jury said that the shot went out of target, which certainly I don't believe, because Rahi is a very experienced shooter, and it could be something else. Let the jury test what it is or otherwise everything was going well,” he added.With five trap medal events still to come, India can add to its shooting tally. But with the likes of Manu unable to convert multiple medal opportunities, the discipline’s overall performance in Aichi-Nagoya has so far fallen well short of the extraordinary returns from Hangzhou.
Article Summary: Double olympic medallist manu bhaker will return from the asian games 2026 without a medal after competing in four events. The 24-year-old could not convert her four medal opportunities into a podium finish. India had won 22 shooting medals, including seven gold, at the hangzhou asian games in 2023.

Article Title: Meet Sister Stephanie Baliga: Once an aspiring elite runner, she became a nun and raised over $2.6 million through the Chicago Marathon; she’s still running to help families in need
Article Text:
Sister Stephanie Baliga turned her passion for running into a mission to help families in need. (Photo: WTTW/Mission of Our Lady of Angels)

Sister Stephanie’s journey from running to religious life

Sister Stephanie Baliga has raised over $2.6 million through the Chicago Marathon. (Photo: WTTW)

Her running now helps feed hundreds of families

Every mile matters: Sister Stephanie Baliga continues running to support a Chicago food pantry. (Photo: Mission of Our Lady of Angels)

Marathon fundraising helped sustain the pantry

Team OLA prepares for another Chicago Marathon

Sister Stephanie Baliga’s marathon journey has helped raise millions for families in need. (Photo: Mission of Our Lady of Angels)

‘The Lord provides’

Sister Stephanie Baliga once dreamed of becoming an elite athlete. Today, the former Division I runner is using that same passion for running to help feed families and senior citizens in her Chicago community.For the past 15 years, Baliga has taken part in the Chicago Marathon as part of the Mission of Our Lady of the Angels (MOLA) charity team. According to MOLA, the marathon team has raised more than $2.6 million between 2011 and 2025, helping support the organisation’s food pantry and community services.This fall, Baliga and nearly 200 members of Team OLA are expected to return for the 16th consecutive Chicago Marathon, with a fundraising goal of $500,000.Baliga began running when she was nine years old, and the sport quickly became central to her identity.“I started running when I was 9, and running became my life,” she told WTTW. “It was how I defined myself and who I was.”As a student-athlete at the University of Illinois, Baliga was the sixth-fastest freshman runner in the nation. She trained for hours each day and was preparing for a potential professional career.At the time, even a marathon time of 2 hours and 53 minutes, fast enough to qualify for the Boston Marathon, did not feel good enough to her.“The challenge of being an elite athlete is that you’re never satisfied with anything you’re doing,” she said.Her path changed when she fractured her foot during her sophomore year. Forced to spend less time running, she turned toward prayer and eventually realised she wanted to devote her life to God.“Jesus saw me for who I was. He was not looking for my straight A’s or my fast running times; he was just seeking to love me wherever I was at,” Baliga said.Baliga eventually found a way to combine her faith with her lifelong passion for running.Through the MOLA marathon team, she has spent the past 15 years raising money for the organisation’s food pantry, which serves hundreds of families every week.“We serve about 400 to 500 families in person every Tuesday and we send about 300 deliveries to senior citizens between Monday and Tuesday each week,” Baliga said. “It totally changed the way I live my life.”Father Bob Lombardo, who opened MOLA, said the organisation serves people regardless of their faith.“As we like to say, we do what we do because we’re Catholic, not because the people we serve are Catholic,” he told WTTW.The charity's marathon efforts have had a significant impact on the food pantry, particularly during a period when demand increased sharply.“The marathon funding was key to expanding the pantry in 2018, 2019 and 2020, and was very key to us sustaining an extremely large pantry during the pandemic,” Baliga said.The team raised about $20,000 during its first marathon. Over the years, that total grew to more than $2.6 million.Reflecting on the amount raised, Baliga said, “It was insane. You’re like, ‘Woah, look at all those zeros! That’s a lot of zeros.’ The Lord provides.”Baliga and nearly 200 Team OLA runners are preparing to run the Chicago Marathon for the 16th consecutive year.The team has set a goal of raising $500,000 this year. Baliga and the team also took part in a half marathon on June 10 as part of their preparations, raising around $16,000.The full marathon team had raised more than $184,000 toward this year’s goal, according to the information provided by MOLA.Supporters have also embraced the team’s mission. Other nuns and supporters have turned out with signs including “You vati-CAN do it” and “May God have mercy on your soles,” along with a cardboard cutout of Pope Leo.MOLA describes Team OLA’s mission as raising awareness and funds for the organisation while offering the time, energy and physical discomfort involved in marathon training in support of the people it serves.For Baliga, the meaning of running has changed dramatically.What once represented a pursuit of faster times and athletic perfection is now a way to help put food on the tables of families and senior citizens.“You’re like, ‘Woah, look at all those zeros! That’s a lot of zeros,’” she said of the team’s fundraising achievement.“The Lord provides,” Baliga added. “God’s will is whatever is in front of you right now.”
Article Summary: Sister stephanie baliga has raised over $2.6 million through the chicago marathon. She is part of the mission of our lady of the angels (mola) charity team. Mola's food pantry serves hundreds of families every week. Nearly 200 team ola runners are preparing to run the chicago marathon for the 16th consecutive year.

Article Title: Nike Alphafly 4 launched with lighter ZoomX LT foam and 10% more energy return
Article Text:
Nike Alphafly 4 are 5% lighter than Alphafly 3

Two foams now sandwich the plate

The upper is designed for tired feet

Nike has launched the Alphafly 4, the newest version of its marathon racing shoe, with changes to nearly every major part. The company says it returns 10% more energy than its predecessor and weighs 5% less in a men's size 8.5.The biggest change is in the midsole. Nike has added a new ZoomX LT foam, which it says is up to 17% lighter than standard ZoomX and offers 8% more energy return. The shoe goes on early, limited sale on nike.com from today, September 17, with wider availability on nike.com and at select stores from October 29.ZoomX LT doesn't fully replace regular ZoomX. Nike layers the two foams above and below the carbon-fibre Flyplate, which keeps the Alphafly's signature propulsive scoop. The plate adds stability and guides a smooth forward roll, which should help runners hold a steady cadence. Up front, dual Air Zoom units have been retuned to work alongside the foam and plate at push-off. A lightweight Fast Shot outsole handles grip.The new Atomknit upper is seamless and breathable. It uses zoned midfoot cables, an integrated heel unit and a molded sock liner to hold the foot securely over long distances.Nike says development drew on athlete feedback across Alphafly generations, learnings from Project Dreamweaver, and extensive women's trials. Emily Farina, Senior Principal, Running Footwear, Nike Sport Research Lab, said the team studied how fatigue changes running mechanics."Our goal was simple: create a shoe that helps athletes feel more confident and capable deep into the race," she said.Nike athlete Addisu Gobena has already tested that claim. He wore the Alphafly 4 to a course-record marathon win in Sydney, and said he trusted the shoe when the race got difficult.
Article Summary: Nike alphafly 4 is the newest version of its marathon racing shoe. The company says it returns 10% more energy than its predecessor and weighs 5% less in a men's size 8.5. Nike has added a new zoomx lt foam, which it says is up to 17% lighter than standard zoomx.

Article Title: Asian Games: How a rare, inexplicable miss by Rahi Sarnobat cost India a 25m pistol team medal
Article Text:
India's Rahi Sarnobat competes during the rapid stage of the women's 25m pistol qualification event. (PTI Photo)

How one miss changed India’s medal prospects

Esha Singh salvages an individual silver

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India were left ruing a costly and extraordinary lapse by experienced shooter Rahi Sarnobat after a rare miss in the women’s 25m pistol team event derailed their medal hopes at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya on Monday. Sarnobat’s shot yielded zero points in the fourth series, a setback that proved decisive as India finished fifth, outside the medal positions.The Indian trio of Esha Singh Manu Bhaker and Sarnobat combined for a score of 1727-56x in the team competition. China won gold with 1743-68x, while South Korea (1735-65x) and Chinese Taipei (1734-48x) took silver and bronze, respectively.For Sarnobat, a former Asian Games gold medallist, the incident was particularly difficult to explain. The shooter herself admitted that she had never experienced anything similar in her career."This is the first time that something like this has happened in my career and I do not know how it happened," Sarnobat said.Her unexpected zero in a competition where every shot counts left India with little room to recover and turned what could have been a medal-winning performance into a disappointing fifth-place finish.The women’s 25m pistol event featured both team and individual competitions, with India fielding three experienced shooters in Esha, Manu and Sarnobat. While Esha kept India’s hopes alive in the individual event, the team’s medal ambitions took a major hit during the qualification rounds.Sarnobat endured a difficult fourth series, registering a score of just 39. The series consisted of five shots, and her performance included the rare miss that resulted in zero points. The setback was particularly damaging in a tightly contested competition, where the margin separating the medal-winning teams was relatively small.Sarnobat eventually finished 30th in the individual qualification standings with a score of 568-16x. Her teammates also had contrasting fortunes in the individual event. Esha qualified for the final in eighth place with 580-22x, while Manu narrowly missed out, finishing 11th with 579-18x.India’s final team score of 1727-56x left them 7 points behind bronze medallists Chinese Taipei and just 8 points behind silver medallists South Korea. The gap to the gold-winning Chinese team was 16 points, underlining the impact of the team’s missed opportunities.Sarnobat, who won gold in the women’s 25m pistol at the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta, was among India’s most experienced competitors in the discipline. Her admission that she could not explain the unusual mistake added to the disappointment of a campaign in which India had entered the event with medal aspirations.While India missed out on a team medal, Esha produced a determined performance in the individual event to secure silver after an exceptionally long final.The 21-year-old from Hyderabad, the reigning world number one, fought through five shoot-offs, including three to move into medal contention and two more in the gold-medal contest against China’s Xiao Jiaruixuan.Both shooters finished regulation with scores of 38, forcing another shoot-off to decide the winner. Esha faltered on the final shot, allowing Xiao to take gold by a single shot. North Korea’s Kim Hyon Suk claimed bronze after losing her shoot-off against Esha, finishing with 34 points."Yes, I was under pressure and this is the longest match of my career so far. My arms were aching at the end of it," Esha said after the final.For Manu, meanwhile, the Asian Games ended without an individual medal. The two-time Olympic medallist had already finished fifth in the women’s 10m air pistol event and was unable to qualify for the 25m pistol final.
Article Summary: India finish fifth in women's 25m pistol team event at asian games 2026. Rahi sarnobat's rare miss in the fourth series left india with little room to recover. China won gold with 1743-68x, while south korea and chinese taipei took silver and bronze.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: Pincky Balhara wins her second Asiad medal, adds kurash bronze to 2018 silver
Article Text:
India's Pincky Balhara, right, competes against South Korea's Mo Sumin in the women's 78kg kurash semifinal. (AP Photo)

Balhara’s second Asiad podium finish

From Jakarta silver to Aichi-Nagoya bronze

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India’s Pincky Balhara secured her second Asian Games medal in kurash, clinching bronze in the women’s -78kg category after losing 0-5 to South Korea’s Sumin Mo in the semifinals at Aichi-Nagoya on Monday.The 27-year-old thus added another medal to her Asian Games collection, eight years after winning silver in the women’s -52kg category at the 2018 Jakarta Games, when kurash made its debut at the continental event.Balhara’s latest podium finish also marked India’s third medal in kurash at the Asian Games. The Indian had reached the semifinals with a 3-0 victory over South Korea’s Garam Lim in the quarterfinals.Balhara began her campaign in the quarterfinals against Lim, where she secured a convincing 3-0 victory to book her place in the last four. The Indian produced the decisive score through a ‘Chala’, a scoring move awarded when a competitor throws an opponent but does not demonstrate complete control over the action.Lim, meanwhile, failed to register a point during the contest, allowing Balhara to progress to the semifinals and put herself in contention for another Asian Games medal.However, the Indian could not overcome Mo in the semifinals. The South Korean secured a 5-0 win, ending Balhara’s hopes of reaching the final and leaving her with the bronze medal.Mo earned a ‘Yonbosh’ point during the contest, while Balhara was penalised with a ‘Dakki’. The Indian was unable to recover from the disadvantage as the South Korean controlled the bout to seal her place in the final.Balhara first made her mark at the Asian Games in 2018, when she won silver in the women’s -52kg category in Jakarta. Kurash was introduced to the Games programme that year, giving Indian athletes an opportunity to compete for medals in the Uzbek martial art.Her silver medal was among India's early successes in the discipline, and her latest podium finish underlines her continued presence in the sport at the highest continental level.The Indian contingent added another medal through Balhara’s performance on Monday, taking its overall tally at the Games to 39, comprising four gold, 17 silver and 18 bronze medals.
Article Summary: Pincky balhara won bronze in the women’s -78kg category at aichi-nagoya. The 27-year-old lost 0-5 to south korea's sumin mo in the semifinals. It is the indian's second asian games medal in kurash. She won silver in the same discipline at the 2018 jakarta games.

Article Title: 'Bhai, meri injury ho gayi hai': How Neeraj Chopra's phone call landed Yashvir Singh an Asian Games spot
Article Text:
Yashvir Singh

From surprise call to Asian Games debut

'Asian Games mein bhi ayega'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Yashvir Singh was lying on his bed at his home in Jaipur after a rigorous training session with his father, Rai Singh, when his phone rang.It was Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra Yashvir had no idea why Chopra was calling. He picked up the phone, unaware that the conversation would bring him an opportunity he had not expected - a place in India's Asian Games squad.Chopra had been ruled out of the Asian Games after suffering an ankle ligament injury. During the call, he asked Yashvir to speak to the federation and be ready to take his place in India's javelin squad for the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya."At that time, I was training and was at home. I was resting when I got a call from Neeraj bhai. He told me, ‘Brother, I’ve suffered an injury. Talk to them further so that your name can be considered in my place." Yashvir told TimesofIndia.com."After that, my name was included," he added.The Asian Games call-up came as a surprise to Yashvir, but his recent performances had put him in contention for a place in the squad. Yashvir had won a bronze medal at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow with a personal best of 85.41m. Chopra finished second in the same event.Yashvir's bronze came after a dramatic final throw. Before his last attempt, he spoke to Chopra and then told himself, "aaj to aar ya paar"."Before the competition, he motivated me a lot. We also spoke before my last throw," Yashvir said.He then produced his personal best of 85.41m to finish on the podium.With Chopra out of the Asian Games, Yashvir will join Rohit Yadav in India's men's javelin team. His 85.41m throw in Glasgow has given him confidence, but Yashvir knows he will face another big challenge in Aichi-Nagoya.After seeing his name in the Asian Games squad, Yashvir spoke to Chopra again. The Olympic medallist encouraged him to make the opportunity count.“He told me, ‘You did well at the Commonwealth Games. Now try to do well at the Asian Games too. Try to win a medal and give it your hundred percent”. Yashvir said.Yashvir believes his preparation is on the right track and is hoping to add another medal to his cabinet.“I’ve focused a lot on my technique. I’m physically fit as well. Now I just have to go there and perform. I dream of doing well,” he said.For Yashvir, the opportunity may have come unexpectedly, but he knows what he has to do when he takes the javelin in his hand again - give his best and fight for another medal in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: Yashvir singh called by olympic champion neeraj chopra. Chopra ruled out of asian games with ankle ligament injury. Yashvir had won bronze medal at commonwealth games in glasgow. He will join rohit yadav in india's men's javelin team.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: India’s 44-year wait ends as Sawan Barwal wins silver in men’s marathon
Article Text:
India's Sawan Barwal reacts after his second place finish in the men's marathon at the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026. (AP Photo/Lee Jin-man)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Historic medal for Indian athletics

Sawan Barwal scripted history at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya on Saturday, winning silver in the men’s marathon and ending India’s 44-year wait for a medal in the event. He clocked a personal best of 2:11:37, finishing 48 seconds behind Japan’s Ichitaka Yamashita, who won gold in 2:10:49. China’s Peiyou Feng took bronze with 2:12:13.The marathon started at 4 a.m. IST with 19 runners, including Barwal and fellow Indian Kartik Karkera. Barwal quickly established himself among the leaders and was in second place at the halfway mark with a timing of 1:05:54. He continued to hold his position as the race entered its final stages, reaching the 35-kilometre mark in second.With around seven kilometres left, Barwal was still chasing Yamashita. The Japanese runner eventually opened up a gap, but Barwal maintained his pace and stayed firmly in silver-medal position. He finished with a timing of 2:11:37, securing India’s first Asian Games marathon medal since the 1982 Delhi Games and the country’s first medal in the event on foreign soil.The silver adds to Barwal’s growing record. In April, he broke Shivnath Singh’s 48-year-old national marathon record at the NN Marathon Rotterdam.His latest performance now converts that record-setting form into a major international medal.Barwal’s silver is India’s fourth Asian Games marathon medal. Chhota Singh won gold and Surat Singh Mathur took bronze at the inaugural 1951 Games, while Hosur Kukkappa Seetharan won another bronze in 1982.The other Indian runner, Kartik Karkera, finished 17th among 19 competitors with a time of 2:22:41.
Article Summary: India's sawan barwal won silver in the men's marathon at the 2026 asian games in nagoya. He clocked a personal best of 2:11:37, finishing 48 seconds behind japan’s ichitaka yamashita, who won gold in 2:10:49. It is india's first asian games marathon medal since the 1982 delhi games and the country's first medal in the event on foreign soil.
